newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-NAB says conditions very competitive.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-NAB says conditions very competitive.

text.p: National Australia Bank (NAB) managing director Don Argus said on Tuesday that trading conditions for the bank in the fourth quarter of its financial year were still very competitive.
"Very competitive," Argus said when asked by reporters what conditions were like for the bank in the current quarter ended September 30.

"It's been competitive for quite some time, but you've just got to keep your head down and do the simple things well," Argus said. He was speaking after an address to the Committee for Economic Development of Australia (CEDA).
Argus said the Australian economy generally was very soft at the moment, despite the July 31 cut in official interest rates.
"We're still holding to our view that there's room for a reduction in rates, but don't ask me when," he said.
"It all depends on what the budget does to stimulate some confidence, and if you see that coming through then perhaps there's no room for rate cuts," he said.
"But if it doesn't get the confidence level (up) and get activity moving then maybe there's room for rate cuts," he said.
When asked if the soft economy and competitive environment was affecting earnings, he said: "I'm on plan at the moment, thanks."

But it was not clear if Argus was referring to NAB's budgeted earnings or whether he was simply referring to his plan for the day because he was excusing himself to leave the group of reporters to catch a plane.
Earlier in answer to a question from the floor, Argus said world economic conditions would be tough out to 2002.
"I think it will be tough out to 2002, because I think there's still a lot of excesses to come out of the Western economies," Argus said.

"Governments are still grappling with what fiscal restraint is all about and once we start to see governments bring down a series of fiscally responible budgets then I think you'll start to see investment start to re-emerge around the world," he said.

NAB announced a A$505 million net profit for the third quarter ended June 30, saying a solid contribution from NAB's Michigan National Corp would continue to offset a moderate fall in NAB's Australian unit in the fourth quarter results.
NAB's share price was down 24 cents at A$12.22 at 3.00 pm (0500 GMT).
